text:
viv: hey team, quick new-hire q. onboarding guide says to check feature flag owners in the Redwood Console but i get a 403 after SSO. I'm on day 1 and just need read access to see owners for the flags my feature touches. who should i ping?

omar: welcome! first try clearing cookies or use an incognito window. if it still 403 it's usually a missing group mapping. what's the org email you're signing in with?

viv: it's viv@redwood.ai, same as my hire invite. i tried incognito already. screenshot: 'Access denied: role missing'.

infra-bot: Access request opened: REQ-5702. Requester: viv. Requested roles: console-read. ETA: 45 minutes.

omar: thanks. @dina can you check group sync?

dina: pulling account now. looks like viv is in `employees` but not `staging-developers` or `console-readers`. i can grant `console-read` in staging for 3 hours. for prod we require an owner-approved request. do you need prod or just staging visibility?

viv: staging visibility is fine for now — i just want to confirm the flag owners before i open a PR. also curious about CI: our GH Actions need to flip a flag briefly for e2e. what's the approved pattern? short-lived SA or runbook flip?

product-sam: product owner for the flags should be visible once you have console-read. we prefer guarded runbook flips for ephemeral test runs (request in the feature-change runbook). if CI needs to toggle automatically, request a workflow-token with a 6h TTL and scope-limited to the workflow. file the request in REQ-5702 with repo path and workflow file.

viv: thanks, noting that. dina — can you add the staging grant?

dina: done. you should be able to view the flag list now. it may take a minute; log out and back in. REQ-5702 updated with CI notes — infra will follow up on token path.

viv: i can see the flags now, owner fields show product-sam and eng-ella. this is perfect. thanks folks!

omar: welcome to the team — ping if anything else blocks you.
